steps: Identify the quantity that changes (gas volume, mass, or amount dissolved) and the time.
Use rate = quantity ÷ time, or concentration = mass ÷ volume.
Convert cm³ to dm³ (÷ 1000) before any concentration divide.
State the answer with its unit: cm³/s, g/s or g/dm³.
method_card.title: Rates from Graphs and Concentrations
method_card.content:
Rate of reaction measures how fast a quantity changes: rate = change in quantity ÷ time. The quantity may be gas volume (cm³), mass lost (g), or product made.

On a graph, a steeper curve means a faster reaction; a flat line means it has finished. Mean rate between two points is the change in height divided by the change in time.

Concentration = mass ÷ volume, with volume in dm³. 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³, so divide a cm³ volume by 1000 first.

exam_context.frequency: Common: rate graphs appear frequently on Paper 2

gold.display: The graph shows two reactions using the same chemicals. Calculate the mean rate of Reaction A over the first 10 seconds.

misconceptions.message: Read Reaction A, the red line. At 10 s it reads 24 cm³, giving 24 ÷ 10 = 2.4 cm³/s. The blue line (Reaction B) reads 15 and gives 1.5.
Use only the first 10 seconds, not the whole run. Rate = 24 ÷ 10 = 2.4 cm³/s.

gold.hint: Read Reaction A (red) at 10 s, then divide by 10.

guided_steps.say: Mean rate = change in volume ÷ time. Read Reaction A, the red line, over the first 10 seconds.
guided_steps.hint: Height of the red line above 10 s.

guided_steps.say: Divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 24 cm³, so Reaction A's mean rate is 2.4 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

gold.display: Using the same graph, calculate the mean rate of Reaction B over the first 10 seconds.

misconceptions.message: Read Reaction B, the blue line. At 10 s it reads 15 cm³, giving 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 cm³/s. The red line (Reaction A) reads 24 and gives 2.4.

gold.hint: Read Reaction B (blue) at 10 s, then divide by 10.

guided_steps.say: Same method, but read Reaction B, the blue line, at 10 seconds.
guided_steps.hint: Height of the blue line above 10 s.

guided_steps.say: Divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 15 cm³, so Reaction B's mean rate is 1.5 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

gold.display: Both reactions produce the same total volume (58 cm³). Suggest why Reaction A has a higher initial rate than Reaction B. Which factor could explain this?
options: Reaction A used a higher concentration of acid
Reaction A used a different acid
Reaction A was carried out at a lower temperature

misconceptions.message: Same total volume means the same amount of reactant. A higher starting rate with the same final volume points to a higher concentration: more frequent collisions at the start, but the same total moles of reactant.

gold.hint: Same total gas means the same amount of reactant. What speeds up the start without changing the total?

gold.display: A solution has a concentration of 40 g/dm³. A student needs 8 g of solute. Calculate the volume of solution they need in cm³.

misconceptions.message: Volume = mass ÷ concentration = 8 ÷ 40 = 0.2 dm³. The answer is wanted in cm³, so multiply by 1000: 200 cm³. Leaving it as 0.2 forgets the conversion.
Rearrange concentration = mass ÷ volume to volume = mass ÷ concentration. Divide the mass by the concentration, not the other way round.

gold.hint: Rearrange to volume = mass ÷ concentration, then convert dm³ to cm³ (× 1000).

guided_steps.say: You are given the concentration and the mass, and asked for the volume. Rearrange concentration = mass ÷ volume to volume = mass ÷ concentration.
Divide the mass by the concentration to get the volume in dm³.
The answer is wanted in cm³, so convert: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³.

guided_steps.done: That returns the 40 g/dm³ concentration, so the volume is 200 cm³.
guided_steps.hint: Mass divided by the volume in dm³ should give the concentration.

gold.display: Use the graph. Calculate the overall mean rate for the entire reaction (from 0 s until the reaction finishes at 60 s).

misconceptions.message: The reaction finishes at 60 s, where the curve goes flat. Rate = 42 ÷ 60 = 0.7 cm³/s. Dividing by 70 gives 0.6, but no gas is made after 60 s.
The line is flat from 60 s to 70 s, so the reaction ended at 60 s. Use 60 s, not 70 s.

gold.hint: The reaction finishes at 60 s; divide the final volume by 60.

guided_steps.say: Overall mean rate = total volume ÷ total time. The reaction finishes at 60 s, where the curve goes flat.
guided_steps.hint: Height where the curve levels off.
The reaction ends at 60 s, not 70 s.

guided_steps.say: Divide the total volume by the total time.

guided_steps.done: Back to 42 cm³, so the overall mean rate is 0.7 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the total time.

gold.display: A hydrochloric acid solution has a concentration of 36 g/dm³. A student uses 500 cm³ of this solution. Calculate the mass of HCl dissolved in this volume.

misconceptions.message: Convert 500 cm³ to 0.5 dm³ first. Mass = 36 × 0.5 = 18 g. Multiplying by 500 gives 18000, far too large.
Mass = concentration × volume = 36 × 0.5 = 18 g. Dividing (36 ÷ 0.5 = 72) is the wrong operation.

gold.hint: Convert 500 cm³ to 0.5 dm³, then mass = concentration × volume.

guided_steps.say: You are given the concentration and the volume, and asked for the mass. Rearrange to mass = concentration × volume, with the volume in dm³.
Convert the volume: 500 cm³ ÷ 1000.
Multiply the concentration by the volume.

guided_steps.done: That returns the 36 g/dm³ concentration, so the mass is 18 g.
guided_steps.hint: Mass divided by volume in dm³ gives concentration.

bronze.display: A reaction produces 48 cm³ of gas in 60 seconds. Calculate the mean rate of reaction.

misconceptions.message: Rate = quantity ÷ time = 48 ÷ 60 = 0.8 cm³/s. Dividing time by quantity (60 ÷ 48 = 1.25) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Rate of reaction = amount of gas produced ÷ time. State the equation, then read the two numbers.
guided_steps.hint: Read it straight from the question.
The question gives the time in seconds.

guided_steps.say: Both are already in the right units, so substitute and divide.
guided_steps.hint: Divide the volume by the time.

guided_steps.done: That returns the 48 cm³ given, so the rate is 0.8 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply your rate back by the time.

bronze.display: A reaction produces 35 cm³ of gas in 50 seconds. Calculate the mean rate of reaction.

misconceptions.message: Rate = 35 ÷ 50 = 0.7 cm³/s. Always put the quantity on top and the time underneath.

guided_steps.say: Rate = amount of gas ÷ time. Pull out the two values.
Units are fine, so divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 35 cm³, so the rate is 0.7 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

bronze.display: In a reaction, the mass of a flask decreases by 0.72 g over 120 seconds as gas escapes. Calculate the mean rate of mass loss.

misconceptions.message: Rate = change in mass ÷ time = 0.72 ÷ 120 = 0.006 g/s. Keep the mass on top.

guided_steps.say: Here the quantity is mass lost, not gas volume, but the rule is the same: rate = change in mass ÷ time.
Divide the mass by the time.
guided_steps.hint: A small number, three decimal places.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.72 g, so the rate is 0.006 g/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

bronze.display: 10 g of salt is dissolved in 2 dm³ of water. Calculate the concentration.

misconceptions.message: Concentration = mass ÷ volume = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 g/dm³. Dividing volume by mass (0.2) is the wrong way round.

guided_steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume, with the volume in dm³. Read the two values.

guided_steps.hint: Already in dm³, no conversion needed.

guided_steps.say: Volume is already in dm³, so divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 10 g, so the concentration is 5 g/dm³.

bronze.display: 4 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in 0.5 dm³ of water. Calculate the concentration.

misconceptions.message: Concentration = 4 ÷ 0.5 = 8 g/dm³. Mass goes on top, volume underneath (0.5 ÷ 4 = 0.125 is upside down).

guided_steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume in dm³.
Divide the mass by the volume.
guided_steps.hint: Dividing by 0.5 is the same as doubling.

guided_steps.done: Back to 4 g, so the concentration is 8 g/dm³.

bronze.display: A reaction produces 56 cm³ of gas in 40 seconds. Calculate the mean rate of reaction.

misconceptions.message: Rate = 56 ÷ 40 = 1.4 cm³/s. Quantity on top, time underneath.

guided_steps.say: Rate = amount of gas ÷ time.
Divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 56 cm³, so the rate is 1.4 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

bronze.display: Use the graph. What is the total volume of gas produced by the end of the reaction?
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{read the final volume from the graph}\)

misconceptions.message: The curve levels off at 42 cm³ from 60 s onwards. That flat height is the total gas produced.

guided_steps.say: The reaction is over when the curve stops climbing and goes flat. Read the height there.
guided_steps.pre: Height of the curve at 50 s =

guided_steps.say: If the next reading is the same, the curve has levelled off.

guided_steps.done: 60 s and 70 s both read 42 cm³, so the flat height, 42 cm³, is the total gas made.
guided_steps.hint: The flat height is the total.

bronze.display: 20 g of copper sulfate is dissolved in 0.4 dm³ of water. Calculate the concentration.

misconceptions.message: Concentration = 20 ÷ 0.4 = 50 g/dm³. Mass on top, volume underneath (0.4 ÷ 20 = 0.02 is upside down).

guided_steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume in dm³.
Divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 20 g, so the concentration is 50 g/dm³.

silver.display: Use the graph. Calculate the mean rate of reaction over the first 20 seconds.

misconceptions.message: At 20 s the volume is 22 cm³. Mean rate = 22 ÷ 20 = 1.1 cm³/s.
Divide by the 20 seconds asked for, not the whole run time. Rate = 22 ÷ 20 = 1.1 cm³/s.

guided_steps.say: Mean rate from a graph = change in volume ÷ change in time. Over the first 20 seconds the change starts from zero.
Divide the volume by the time.

guided_steps.done: Back to 22 cm³, so the mean rate is 1.1 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

silver.display: Use the graph. Calculate the mean rate of reaction between 10 s and 30 s.

misconceptions.message: At 10 s volume = 12 cm³, at 30 s volume = 30 cm³.
Use the CHANGE in volume, 30 − 12 = 18 cm³, not the 30 at the end. With the 20 s interval that gives 18 ÷ 20 = 0.9 cm³/s. Using 30 ÷ 20 gives 1.5, which is too fast.

guided_steps.say: Between two times you need the change in volume AND the change in time. Read both heights first.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the earlier height from the later one.

guided_steps.say: The time interval is 30 − 10 = 20 s. Now divide.
guided_steps.hint: Change in volume divided by change in time.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 18 cm³ change, so the mean rate is 0.9 cm³/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time interval.

silver.display: 7.3 g of hydrochloric acid is dissolved in 250 cm³ of water. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

misconceptions.message: Convert 250 cm³ to 0.25 dm³ first. Dividing by 250 straight away gives 0.0292, far too small. Correct: 7.3 ÷ 0.25 = 29.2 g/dm³.
250 cm³ is 0.25 dm³, not 250 dm³. Divide the cm³ by 1000 before dividing the mass.

guided_steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume, and the volume must be in dm³. This one is in cm³, so convert first.
Convert the volume: 1000 cm³ = 1 dm³, so divide by 1000.
guided_steps.hint: Move the decimal point three places.

guided_steps.say: Now divide the mass by the volume in dm³.

guided_steps.done: Back to 7.3 g, so the concentration is 29.2 g/dm³.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply concentration by volume in dm³.

silver.display: 5.85 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 500 cm³ of water. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

misconceptions.message: Convert 500 cm³ to 0.5 dm³ first. Dividing by 500 gives 0.0117, far too small. Correct: 5.85 ÷ 0.5 = 11.7 g/dm³.
500 cm³ = 0.5 dm³. Convert before dividing.

guided_steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume in dm³. The volume is in cm³, so convert.
Convert: divide the cm³ by 1000.
Now divide.

guided_steps.done: Back to 5.85 g, so the concentration is 11.7 g/dm³.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply concentration by volume in dm³.

silver.display: Use the graph. Calculate the mean rate of mass loss over the first 40 seconds.

misconceptions.message: At 40 s the mass lost is 0.28 g. Rate = 0.28 ÷ 40 = 0.007 g/s.

guided_steps.say: Mean rate of mass loss = change in mass ÷ time. Read the blue line at 40 s.
guided_steps.hint: Height of the line above 40 s.

guided_steps.say: Divide the mass by the time.
guided_steps.hint: A small number, three decimal places.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.28 g, so the mean rate is 0.007 g/s.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

silver.display: Use the graph. At what time does the reaction finish? (When the graph becomes flat.)
silver.equation_hint: \(\text{reaction finishes when the line goes flat}\)

misconceptions.message: The mass loss stops changing at 0.48 g. Both 100 s and 120 s read 0.48 g, so the reaction finishes at 100 s.

guided_steps.say: The reaction has finished when the mass loss stops changing, where the curve goes flat. Read the last few points.
If the next point is the same, nothing more is being lost.

guided_steps.done: 100 s and 120 s both read 0.48 g, so no gas escapes after 100 s. The reaction finishes at 100 s.
guided_steps.hint: The first time the value stops rising.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One step: put the numbers straight into rate = quantity ÷ time, or concentration = mass ÷ volume.
problem_bank.silver_description: Read a change off a graph, or convert cm³ to dm³, before you divide.
problem_bank.gold_description: Two moves: rearrange the equation or read the right line, then convert units to finish.

steps.label: Step 1: Read from the graph
steps.content: At t = 0 s, volume = 0 cm³. At t = 20 s, volume = 22 cm³.

worked_examples.question: The graph below shows the volume of gas produced over time. Calculate the mean rate of reaction over the first 20 seconds.
7.3 g of hydrochloric acid is dissolved in 250 cm³ of water. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

bronze.title: Bronze: one equation, straight in
steps: Rate = quantity ÷ time. The quantity can be gas volume (cm³), mass lost (g), or product formed.
Concentration = mass ÷ volume, with the volume in dm³.
Read both numbers from the question, divide, and add the unit (cm³/s, g/s or g/dm³).

example.question: A reaction makes 45 cm³ of gas in 90 s. Find the mean rate.

silver.title: Silver: convert or read a change first
steps: From a graph, mean rate = change in quantity ÷ change in time. Read both points, subtract, then divide.
For concentration, convert the volume: cm³ ÷ 1000 = dm³ before dividing.
One extra step before the divide, that is all silver adds.

example.question: 8.5 g of solute is dissolved in 500 cm³. Find the concentration in g/dm³.

gold.title: Gold: rearrange and convert
steps: Rearrange for what is asked: volume = mass ÷ concentration, or mass = concentration × volume.
Convert between cm³ and dm³ as the final step (× 1000 or ÷ 1000).
For two-curve graphs, read the right line, then divide by the time interval.

example.question: A solution is 50 g/dm³. How many cm³ hold 5 g?

opener.label: Before any equations
opener.display:
A fizzy tablet in water:
30 cm³ of gas bubbles up in 10 seconds.

steps.say: Drop a fizzy vitamin tablet in water and watch the bubbles. No chemistry needed yet.
steps.pre: It makes 30 cm³ of gas in 10 seconds. Each second it makes about
steps.hint: Share the 30 cm³ out over the 10 seconds: 30 ÷ 10.

steps.say: That number, gas made each second, is the rate of reaction. You just did rate = amount ÷ time.
steps.pre: A stronger tablet makes the same 30 cm³ in only 6 seconds. Its rate is

steps.say: Faster reaction, bigger rate. On a graph the gas climbs more steeply, and reading a value off the graph then dividing by the time is the whole skill.

bronze.label: Together: your first one
bronze.display: A reaction produces 60 cm³ of gas in 30 seconds. Calculate the mean rate of reaction.

steps.say: Rate of reaction = amount of gas produced ÷ time. Write it down, then read the numbers.
Both units are fine, so divide.

steps.done: Back to 60 cm³. The mean rate is 2 cm³/s, gas over time. That is the whole bronze move.
steps.hint: Multiply the rate by the time.

silver.label: Together: the silver move
silver.display: 9.2 g of solute is dissolved in 400 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

steps.say: Concentration = mass ÷ volume, but the volume must be in dm³ and this one is in cm³. The conversion is the new silver step.
Convert the volume: 1000 cm³ = 1 dm³, so divide by 1000.
Now divide the mass by the volume in dm³.

steps.done: Back to 9.2 g. The concentration is 23 g/dm³. Converting the volume first was the whole point.
steps.hint: Multiply concentration by volume in dm³.

gold.label: Together: the gold move
gold.display: A solution has a concentration of 25 g/dm³. A student needs 5 g of solute. Calculate the volume of solution needed in cm³.

steps.say: Here you rearrange AND convert, the gold combination. Concentration = mass ÷ volume rearranges to volume = mass ÷ concentration.
Divide the mass by the concentration for the volume in dm³.

steps.done: That returns the 25 g/dm³ concentration. The volume is 200 cm³. Rearrange, then convert.
steps.hint: Mass ÷ volume in dm³ should give the concentration.
